{{Short description|American quantitative psychologist}}
'''Linda M. Collins''' is an American quantitative psychologist who is a professor of global public health at [[New York University]].  

== Life ==
Collins earned a B.A. in psychology at the [[University of Connecticut]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Linda Collins {{!}} NYU School of Global Public Health |url=https://publichealth.nyu.edu/faculty/linda-collins |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=publichealth.nyu.edu |language=en}}</ref> She received a Ph.D. in [[quantitative psychology]] from the [[University of Southern California]].<ref name=":0" />

Collins was a tenured faculty member at the University of Southern California.<ref name=":0" /> She was a distinguished professor of human development and family studies at [[Pennsylvania State University]].<ref name=":0" /> At [[New York University]], she is a professor of global public health in the department of social and behavioral sciences.<ref name=":0" />

Collins is an elected fellow of the [[American Psychological Association]], [[Association for Psychological Science]], and the [[Society of Behavioral Medicine]].<ref name=":0" /> She served as president of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]] and the [[Society for Prevention Research]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-28 |title=Optimization of Prevention Interventions Using MOST: State of the Science and Future Directions {{!}} NIH Office of Disease Prevention Website |url=https://prevention.nih.gov/education-training/methods-mind-gap/optimization-prevention-interventions-using-most-state-science-and-future-directions |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=prevention.nih.gov |language=en |archive-date=2024-04-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240429001322/https://prevention.nih.gov/education-training/methods-mind-gap/optimization-prevention-interventions-using-most-state-science-and-future-directions |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research and contributions ==
Dr. Collins is known for her work on the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST), which integrates concepts from engineering, behavioral science, multivariate statistics, health economics, and decision analysis.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-72206-1 |title=Optimization of Behavioral, Biobehavioral, and Biomedical Interventions |series=Statistics for Social and Behavioral Sciences |date=2018 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-72206-1|isbn=978-3-319-72205-4 }}</ref> MOST aims to enhance intervention effectiveness, affordability, scalability, and efficiency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Webadmin-ioi |title=Overview of MOST |url=https://cadio.org/intervention-optimization/overview-of-most/ |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=Center for Advancement and Dissemination of Intervention Optimization |language=en-US}}</ref> She has applied MOST in diverse areas, including HIV,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gwadz |first1=Marya Viorst |last2=Collins Her research has received funding from institutions such as the [[National Institute on Drug Abuse]] (NIDA), the [[National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism]] (NIAAA), the [[National Cancer Institute]] (NCI), the [[National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases]] (NIDDK), and the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF).<ref>{{Cite web |title=RePORT ⟩ RePORTER |url=https://reporter.nih.gov/search/6EDL_k5fGEC__6zffm7FKQ/projects?fy=2024;2023;2022;2021;2020;2019;2018;2017;2016;2015;2014;2013;2012;2011;2010;2009;2008;2007;2006;2005;2004;2003;2002;2001;2000;1999;1998&shared=true |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=reporter.nih.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NSF Award Search: Award # 8403126 - Longitudinal Scaling Methodology |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=8403126&HistoricalAwards=false |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref>

Collins has published extensively in journals across behavioral sciences, quantitative methodology, medicine, and engineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Linda M. Collins |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=670cSfUAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> She has given over 150 invited presentations on MOST worldwide.<ref name=":0" /> Collaborating with Dr. Kate Guastaferro, she developed two massive open online courses on intervention optimization and MOST.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MOST from a Conceptual Perspective |url=https://www.coursera.org/learn/most-conceptual-perspective |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=Coursera |language=en}}</ref>
